name: Calcium chloride
executiveSummary: Concentrated Ca²⁺ salt. Adult arrest: **1 g (10 mL of 10%)** IV/IO. Pediatrics: **0.1–0.2 mL/kg** (common hyperK max **3 mL**). NICU: **20 mg/kg** slow IV. More elemental Ca/mL than gluconate — do not interchange mL for mL.
indications:
## Indications

- Symptomatic hypocalcemia; hyperkalemia with ECG changes; Ca²⁺-blocker overdose (protocols).
- Arrest with suspected reversible cause (hyperK / hypoCa / Ca-blocker overdose).

## Precautions

- Extravasation → severe necrosis; prefer central line.
- **Incompatible with bicarbonate, phosphate, and sulfate** (precipitates).
- Do not interchange mL for mL with gluconate.

> Ampule 10%: **100 mg/mL** CaCl₂ ≈ **1.4 mEq Ca²⁺/mL**.

adulto.presentation: Ampule 10 mL of 10% (~13.6 mEq Ca /10 mL).
adulto.dose: Arrest / severe hyperK: **10 mL (1 g)** IV/IO; may repeat. Hypocalcemia: **5–10 mL (0.5–1 g)** slow IV every 6 h per ionized Ca.
adulto.administration: Slow IV/IO (< **0.5–1 mL/min** push); for infusion dilute ~**20 mg/mL** and infuse ~1 h.

pediatrico.dose: Symptomatic hypocalcemia: **0.1–0.2 mL/kg** (**0.14–0.28 mEq/kg**) every 4–6 h. HyperK: **0.3 mL/kg** (common max **3 mL**/dose).

neonatal.dose: **20 mg/kg** (= **0.2 mL/kg** of 10%) slow IV in arrest/symptomatic hypocalcemia; may repeat per response.
neonatal.administration: Central IV preferred; slow with monitoring.

stability:
## Stability

- Do not mix with HCO₃⁻/PO₄³⁻ in the same line.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Bradycardia, hypotension if rapid; necrosis from extravasation; hypercalcemia.

bibliography.citation: Hospital Garrahan. Formulario — cloruro de calcio.
